## Recommended first contact: American University Washington College of Law

Start with **AUWCL** if public-interest/public-service work genuinely fits your goals. Its PIPS program is a **three-year, full-tuition** scholarship, so it has the largest potential funding impact—and its application deadline is **January 31, 2027, at 11:59 PM EST**, earlier than the general-admission priority deadline. The tradeoff is that it requires a separate application, so act on it first rather than treating it as a later financial-aid task.

**Next move:** use the live PIPS application form:  
https://american.co1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6FMJcuOCtqeRJiu

The form begins by asking for your LSAC number and email. AUWCL’s application-process page says you need the general JD application and PIPS application completed by the deadline; it also calls for the PIPS essays/resume and lists a recommendation letter as optional but strongly recommended. AUWCL says awards are made from March through mid-April.

**Plain-English PIPS summary:** It is designed to fund incoming full-time JD students who have strong academics and a real commitment and career plan for public-interest or public-service work after law school. It provides tuition coverage for all three years, while offering programmatic support as well.

I left AUWCL’s dedicated PIPS scholarship page open in its own tab, as requested. I also left its application/selection-details page and live application form available.

## Your simple outreach plan

### 1) University of Maryland Carey Law — request info + attend a webinar
- **Request materials:** On Carey’s official Contact Admissions page, use **“Request Information: JD Applicants.”**
- **Direct admissions contact:** `admissions@law.umaryland.edu` | **(410) 706-3492**
- **Office hours:** Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM.
- **Online event to consider:** **JD Admissions 101 Webinar — Thursday, August 13, 2026, 12:00 pm–1:00 pm.** The webinar page provides a “Register here” link. If that midday slot is inconvenient, the same page also lists an evening session on **Thursday, September 3, 2026, 5:00 pm–6:00 pm**.
- **Next move:** submit the JD request-information form today, then register for the webinar time that works best and email one or two specific questions in advance.

I left the official Carey **JD Webinars** event-details page open in its own tab.

### 2) University of Baltimore School of Law — schedule a counselor call
- **Best direct option:** the school’s Visit page links to a **30-minute phone or Zoom appointment with an admissions counselor** for in-depth questions.
- **Registration form:** https://forms.lsac-unite.org/5810/UBaltLawPhoneCallFall2026.html
- The live registration form offers **30-minute phone-call slots** and asks for your name, LSAC-associated email, cell number, LSAC number, and expected entry year. It displays times in Eastern Time.
- **Fallback contact from the same official visit page:** `lawadmissions@ubalt.edu` | **410-837-4459**, business hours **8:30am–4:30pm**.
- **Also available:** a Fall Virtual Open House on **Tuesday, October 27, 2026, 6:00–7:00 PM ET**, via Zoom; no registration is required and the password is **UBaltLaw**.
- **Next move:** reserve the 30-minute call and prepare questions on admissions fit, scholarships, and your intended practice area.

I left UBalt’s official **Visit the School of Law** admissions/meeting page open so you can compare it beside Carey’s page.

### Practical priority order
1. **AUWCL first:** time-sensitive separate application for a potentially transformative full-tuition PIPS award.
2. **Carey second:** very low-friction JD information request plus multiple scheduled virtual admissions webinars.
3. **UBalt third:** easiest option for a personalized conversation—book the structured 30-minute counselor call once you have your core comparison questions ready.

This ordering assumes you have genuine public-interest/public-service career interest. If you do not, move Carey to first: its JD request form, direct admissions email/phone, and recurring virtual webinar choices make it the simplest general-admissions outreach route.
